value.body: A two-year master's in planning, with specialisations such as urban, regional, transport, housing, environmental or infrastructure planning. Students work on studios, surveys and real planning projects for towns and regions.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Usually a B.Arch, B.Plan or B.E./B.Tech (civil); some programmes also accept geography or economics postgraduates. Admission is through institute entrance tests and interviews, with some institutes using GATE (Architecture & Planning) scores.

value.title: At a glance
items: A small field — far fewer seats than most master's programmes.
Employers include state town-planning departments, development authorities, municipal bodies, smart-city companies and consultancies.
Government town-planner posts are recruited through state PSCs and often ask for a planning degree.
